entities.summary:
A Storm of Swords is a seminal work of epic fantasy that redefined the genre in the late 20th century. George R.R. Martin's magnum opus, published between 1999 and 2000, consists of 784 pages and 95 chapters, immersing readers in the brutal world of Westeros. The novel's intricate narrative explores the complexities of power, loyalty, and survival in a realm where the Seven Kingdoms are torn apart by civil war and external threats. Through its richly detailed characters and meticulous plotting, A Storm of Swords offers a nuanced commentary on human nature, revealing both the beauty and the darkness that define us.

This literary achievement has left an indelible mark on the fantasy genre, influencing countless authors and inspiring a devoted fan base. The book's impact extends beyond the realm of fiction, with its exploration of complex moral themes and its portrayal of the devastating consequences of war resonating deeply with readers worldwide.

As a cultural touchstone, A Storm of Swords has been adapted into various forms of media, including television and video games, cementing its place in the collective consciousness. The novel's significance extends beyond its artistic merit, serving as a reflection of our own time's preoccupations with power, identity, and the human condition.

Their legacy is studied through the lens of historical causation.", "summary": "A Storm of Swords is the third novel in George R. R. Martin's A Song of Ice and Fire epic fantasy series, published on 8 August 2000 by Bantam Books — widely regarded by fans and critics as the best volume in the series, and the source of the series' most famous narrative event: the Red Wedding (the massacre of Robb Stark, his mother Catelyn Tully-Stark, and the Northern army at the wedding feast of Edmure Tully). With over 10 million copies sold, it is the best-selling volume of the series. A Storm of Swords covers the aftermath of the War of the Five Kings — the deaths of Robb Stark, Renly Baratheon, and Stannis's defeat at Blackwater — while advancing the story of Daenerys Targaryen's conquest of Essos, Jon Snow's experiences beyond the Wall with the wildlings, Tyrion Lannister's survival after the Battle of the Blackwater, and Jaime Lannister's transformation following the loss of his sword hand.

The Red Wedding — in which Walder Frey and Roose Bolton massacre Robb Stark and his Northern army at the wedding feast under the sacred protection of guest right — is the single most shocking narrative event in the A Song of Ice and Fire series and one of the most famous plot twists in the history of popular fiction. Its combination of narrative misdirection (the apparent security of guest right, the apparent political resolution of the Frey-Tully wedding), the scale of the betrayal, and the deaths of what had been presented as the main protagonist's family — coming after the series had already killed its apparent first protagonist (Ned Stark in book 1) — established Martin's narrative as uniquely willing to subvert the reader's expectations of heroic fantasy. The Red Wedding's HBO adaptation in Season 3 (Episode 9, 'The Rains of Castamere', directed by David Nutter) produced one of the most widely shared collective audience shock reactions in television history.

A Storm of Swords also contains the most concentrated sequence of major character transformations in the series: Jaime Lannister's redemption arc (the Oathbreaker who becomes the Oathkeeper), Arya Stark's journey toward the Faceless Men, Sansa's escape from King's Landing, Joffrey's assassination at his own wedding (the Purple Wedding), and Jon Snow's election as Lord Commander of the Night's Watch. **Paragraph 1 — Identity & Significance**: A Storm of Swords is a seminal novel in the realm of modern fantasy literature, published in 2000 by renowned author George R. R. Martin.

This epic tale, set in the world of Westeros, explores the complexities of human nature, power struggles, and the intricacies of character development, all against the backdrop of a global conflict that reshapes the fate of the Seven Kingdoms.

Key figures involved include the Starks, Lannisters, and Baratheons, who navigate the treacherous landscape of alliances, betrayals, and bloody battles.
